questions.question: Why should journalists avoid technical jargon in news stories?
questions.solution_html:
• According to Press Council of India, a journalist should maintain follow certain
  • ethical norms such as
  • a) Accuracy and fairness: A journalist must inform, and comment on matters of
  • public interest, in a fair, accurate unbiased and decent manner. Inaccuracy and
  • personal remarks should always be avoided.
  • b) Prepublication Verification: Verification and checking of news before
  • publication is all the more necessary where its publication, and the comments based
  • thereon, can create complications.
  • c) Caution Against Defamatory Writings: Newspapers should not publish anything
  • which is per se defamatory or libelous against any individual or organization, unless
  • after due care and checking, they have sufficient reason to believe that it is true and
  • that its publication will be for public good.
  • d) Privacy: Intrusion or invasion on the privacy of individuals is not permissible
  • unless outweighed by genuine overriding public interest. While publishing names or
  • pictures of victims of sex crimes, great caution should be exercised.
  • e) Eschew Suggestive Guilt: Newspapers should eschew suggestive guilt by
  • association. They should not name or identify the family or relatives or associates of a
  • person convicted or accused of a crime when they are totally innocent and a reference
  • to them is not relevant to the matter reported.
  • f) Corrections: When any factual error or mistake is detected or confirmed, the
  • newspaper should publish the correction promptly, with due prominence and with an
  • apology or expression of regret in a case of serious lapse. He should also give due
  • weightage to the right of reply and to the letters to the Editor.
  • g) Communal Reports: Proper verification must be done before publishing reports
  • regarding communal clashes or disputes. The report should not vitiate the situation.
  • Instead, it should aim at soothing the ruffled feelings.
  • h) Sensational Headings: Sensational headings should be avoided. Headlines should
  • conform to the contents of news stories. They should be clear, unambiguous and
  • authentic.
  • i) Eschew Vulgarity and Obscenity: Obscene and vulgar items should be done away
  • with as these offend the public's good taste. Also, never glorify violence.
  • j) Avoid Crass Commercialism: In order to make profits, a newspaper should not
  • throw the ethics and journalistic values to the winds. Instead, it should try to create a
  • suitable equilibrium between objectivity and commercialism.
  • k) Avoid Caste, Religion or Community Disclosures: In general, a newspaper
  • should, not identify a person with his caste, religion or community.
  • l) Respect Confidence: If information is received from a source confidentially, the
  • confidence should be respected.
questions.source_exam: Official Model Question Paper (FYUGP 2024
questions.final_answer: confidence should be respected.

questions.question: Classify the types of news based on geographical location using relevant examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Classify the types of news based on geographical location using relevant examples.
  • News can be broadly classified by geographical scope into local, national, and international
  • news, each focusing on events within a specific boundary. Local news, such as a story about a new
  • town council ordinance, focuses on community affairs, while national news covers issues affecting an
  • entire country, like a presidential election. International news reports on significant events occurring
  • globally, such as treaty negotiations between multiple countries.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: globally, such as treaty negotiations between multiple countries.

questions.question: Compare and contrast the characteristics of print, broadcast, and online news media
questions.solution_html:
• Benefits of the Inverted Pyramid Style
  • • Prioritizes Crucial Information: This style ensures that the most important
  • information is delivered first. The lead contains the who, what, when, where, and
  • why, allowing readers to grasp the essential details quickly.
  • • Facilitates Quick Editing: Editors can easily trim stories from the bottom if space is
  • limited without losing the core information. This makes it highly practical for both
  • print and digital media.
  • • Enhances Reader Engagement: By presenting the key points right away, the
  • inverted pyramid style captures the reader's attention immediately. This is especially
  • important in an era where readers have shorter attention spans.
  • • Improves Search Engine Optimization (SEO): Online, this style helps with SEO as
  • it aligns with algorithms that prioritize articles where crucial information appears
  • early. It ensures that the content is indexed efficiently, making it more discoverable.
  • • Supports Breaking News: In fast-paced news situations, the inverted pyramid allows
  • for quick dissemination of vital information. It caters to audiences who need
  • immediate updates on ongoing events.
  • Why It Is Regarded as Efficient
  • • Clarity and Brevity: The inverted pyramid style ensures that the news is clear and
  • concise, which is critical when communicating urgent or complex issues.
  • • Flexibility for Updates: As new information comes in, updates can be added to the
  • existing article without restructuring the entire piece, maintaining the narrative's
  • integrity.
  • • Audience-Centric: This approach respects the reader's time, delivering the most
  • critical information upfront and allowing them to decide whether to read further for
  • additional details.
questions.source_exam: Official Model Question Paper (FYUGP 2024
questions.final_answer: additional details.

questions.question: Analyze the legal challenges presented by AI-generated media (audio, video, images) that realistically depict non-existent events.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the legal challenges presented by AI-generated media (audio, video, images) that
  • realistically depict non-existent events.
  • General answer - AI-generated media depicting non-existent events presents significant legal
  • challenges, primarily concerning defamation, copyright, and the right of publicity. If this media falsely
  • portrays a person in a negative light, it can lead to defamation lawsuits and, if a likeness is used
  • without permission, may violate their right of publicity. Furthermore, the use of existing copyrighted
  • works to train AI models and generate new content raises complex issues regarding fair use and
  • intellectual property infringement.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: intellectual property infringement.

questions.question: Describe how you would prepare to cover an important political speech of a national leader
questions.solution_html:
• . Describe how you would prepare to cover an important political speech of a national
  • leader
  • To cover an important political speech, I would first conduct thorough research on the
  • leader's past statements, current policy positions, and the context surrounding the speech to
  • anticipate key themes. During the speech, I would actively listen for major announcements, shifts in
  • tone, or quotes that summarize the speech's main message, while also observing the audience's
  • reaction. Finally, I would immediately begin analyzing the speech's significance and its potential
  • political impact to frame my reporting accurately.

questions.final_answer: political impact to frame my reporting accurately.

questions.question: Evaluate the significance of specialized reporting in an era of information overload.
questions.solution_html:
• Informed Coverage: Specialized reporters have deep knowledge in their fields
  • allowing them to provide accurate and comprehensive coverage. They explain
  • complex topics clearly, offering valuable insights and detailed accounts that enrich
  • understanding.
  • Credibility and Trust: Experts in journalism build trust through their authoritative
  • knowledge on specific subjects like finance, technology, health, and environmental
  • issues. They verify facts and debunk falsehoods, ensuring reliable information amid rising
  • misinformation.
  • Audience Targeting: Specialized reporting tailors content to specific audience segments
  • addressing unique concerns and preferences. This approach builds a loyal, engaged
  • community.
  • Curating Content: Specialized journalists sift through vast information, highlighting key
  • findings that matter most. For example, a medical journalist identifies significant research
  • breakthroughs, helping readers focus on essential information.
questions.source_exam: Official Model Question Paper (FYUGP 2024
questions.final_answer: breakthroughs, helping readers focus on essential information.

questions.question: Explain the role of multimedia in enhancing a news story. Provide examples to illustrate your points. (2 x 15 = 30 Marks)
questions.solution_html:
• Three national news agencies
  • o THE PRESS TRUST OF INDIA (PTI) is the largest news agency in India. It
  • was founded on August 27, 1947, and began operations in February 1949. PTI
  • is a non-profit cooperative owned by more than 450 Indian newspapers. It
  • provides news coverage in both English and Hindi and has correspondents in
  • major cities and capitals around the world. PTI is headquartered in New Delhi
  • Aveek Sarkar: chairman of PTI
  • o UNITED NEWS OF INDIA (UNI): The second-largest news agency in India
  • Founded on December 19, 1959. It began its commercial operations on March 21
  • 1961. UNI provides news coverage in multiple languages, including English
  • Hindi, Urdu, and Kannada. UNI was established to provide a second news agency
  • in India, acting as a corrective to the Press Trust of India (PTI). It was sponsored
  • by eight leading newspapers, including The Hindu, The Times of India, and The
  • Statesman.
  • o Asian News International (ANI): Founded: 1971 by Prem Prakash.
  • Services: Provides syndicated multimedia news feeds, including text news, TV
  • programs, and multimedia content. It covers a wide range of topics such as
  • politics, business, sports, entertainment, health, technology, and travel.
  • Three international news agencies
  • o Associated Press (AP): Founded in 1846 in New York, AP is one of the
  • largest and most respected news agencies globally. It provides news coverage
  • in multiple languages and has a vast network of journalists and bureaus in
  • nearly 120 countries. Operates AP Radio Network and AP Television News
  • (APTN), a global video news agency.
  • o Reuters: Paul Reuters founded it in 1851.Thomson Reuters Corporation, a
  • multinational media conglomerate, currently owns Reuters with its
  • headquarters in London. Coverage in over 16 languages.
  • o Agence France-Presse (AFP): A French international news agency
  • headquartered in Paris, France. Founded in 1835 as Havas, it is the world's
  • oldest news agency. Founder: Charles-Louis Havas.
questions.source_exam: Official Model Question Paper (FYUGP 2024
questions.final_answer: Three national news agencies
